we show that quantum fluctuations can be controlled and that the coherent state of a two level atom in a superconducting cavity can be controlled.
we have demonstrated that it is possible to compensate the influence of quantum vacuum fluctuations on an atom by means of a coherent feedback field.

the quantum fluctuations of the vacuum electromagnetic field can be compensated for and the decoherence associated to spontaneous emission can be suppressed by balanced homodyning and coherent feedback.

quantum information processing and quantum control of open quantum systems.
the control of quantum fluctuations and the suppression of decoherence.
the development of a new approach to the quantum control of atomic systems by means of a coherent feedback field.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the quantum control of the atom is achieved by the compensation of quantum fluctuations in a coherent feedback field.
the coherent state of a quantum system can be fully controlled and stabilized.

the quantum feedback control scheme is able to compensate the quantum fluctuations of the field, which are the origin of spontaneous emission and decoherence, and thus, to stabilize the quantum state of the atomic qubit.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
quantum fluctuations are not only a nuisance but also a valuable resource for the quantum control of a two level system.
we have shown that the quantum vacuum can be used as a quantum resource.
quantum control can be achieved by compensation of quantum effects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the quantum fluctuations in the vacuum can be used to control the quantum state of a system.
it is possible to control a quantum system by compensating for the influence of the quantum fluctuations of the environment.
the compensation scheme is not only applicable to a single atom, but also to any quantum system with a single quantum degree of freedom.
